The diagram is a \(3\times 3\) grid of points.

- At least \(3\) points must be removed: if only \(2\) were removed, then among the \(3\) horizontal rows, at least one row would still contain all \(3\) of its points, giving three collinear points.
- Three removals are enough: remove the three points on a main diagonal (top-left, center, bottom-right). Then every row and column has at most \(2\) remaining points, and the other diagonal is also broken because its center point was removed.

Therefore, the minimum number of points to remove is

\[
\boxed{3\text{ points}}
\]
